summary: A dense, cutthroat tile-placement game where you build linked civilizations along rivers and fight brutal internal and external conflicts to install or topple leaders. It rewards ruthless, calculated aggression and balanced development over any single strong suit, since your final score is only as high as your weakest of four categories.
praised: Deep, ruthless strategic depth that rewards long-term planning
Conflict system (internal and external) is tense and meaningful
Elegant, tightly interlocking rules with no wasted mechanisms
High replayability due to shifting alliances and board states
criticised: Steep learning curve and rules that are hard to fully grasp on a first play
Can feel mean and confrontational, alienating players who dislike direct conflict
Downtime and analysis paralysis in higher player counts
Red (conflict) tiles and combat math are unintuitive at first

interaction.kind: direct conflict, blocking, and area control

scoring.why: The winner is whoever has the highest score in their single weakest of the four leader categories, forcing balanced growth across all colors rather than a dominant specialty.
